analysis.title: Atlas Energy Solutions (AESI): 3Q26 First Take: EBITDA Miss vs GS/Consensus; Focus on BTM Contracts and Sand Pricing on Call
key_insights: AESI reported 3Q26 EBITDA of $30 mil, below the GS estimate of $39 mil and FactSet consensus of $36 mil.
Revenue was 4.3% below GS at $268 mil vs $280 mil. Service Sales were 8.8% below GS, Rental Sales 12.8% below GS, and Product Sales 6.4% above GS.
Sand volumes of 5.40 mil tons matched GS. Implied pricing of $18.13/ton was above the GS estimate of $17.06/ton but down 10.9% from $20.35/ton in 3Q25.
The company prioritized sand pricing during the quarter, which slightly reduced 3Q volumes.
For 2027, the company has line of sight to more than 23 mil tons allocated and expects sequential improvement across all business lines in 4Q.
Company guided 4Q Adjusted EBITDA to $40-50 mil. The call is expected to focus on behind-the-meter (BTM) power contracts and sand pricing.
EBITDA margin was 11.3% vs the GS estimate of 13.9%, and down from 16.9% in 2Q26 and 15.5% in 3Q25.
Free cash flow was -$161 mil vs the GS estimate of -$28 mil. EPS was -$0.36 vs the GS estimate of -$0.29.
GS rates AESI Sell with a 12-month price target of $11 (33.7% upside to the $8.23 close on 2 Nov 2026), based on a 4.5x through-cycle EV/EBITDA multiple.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell rating and $11 target on a 4.5x through-cycle EV/EBITDA multiple. The 3Q26 EBITDA of $30 mil missed GS at $39 mil and consensus at $36 mil.

earnings_insights: AESI 3Q26 reported EBITDA $30 mil vs GS est $39 mil and FactSet consensus est $36 mil (reported 2 Nov 2026).
3Q26 total revenue $268 mil reported vs GS est $280 mil, 2Q26A $293 mil and 3Q25A $260 mil.
3Q26 reported EPS -$0.36 vs GS est -$0.29, 2Q26A -$0.20 and 3Q25A -$0.19.
3Q26 reported free cash flow -$161 mil vs GS est -$28 mil.
4Q26 company guidance for Adjusted EBITDA is $40-50 mil.
GS estimates for FY12/26E: revenue $1,128.6 mil, EBITDA $168.4 mil, EPS -$1.11. FY12/27E: revenue $1,329.7 mil, EBITDA $302.1 mil, EPS -$0.70.
risk_factors: Upside from higher pricing and volume in behind-the-meter power contracts than anticipated.
